title: Explicit and Implicit Modeling via Dual-Path Transformer for Behavior Set-informed Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Behavior set-informed sequential recommendation must model complex, personalized behavior dependencies and behavior-linked user-interest arousal without relying on explicit contextual associations.

gap.claim: Existing multi-behavior sequential recommendation work is concentrated in e-commerce, while conventional label-formatted behavior data carries limited information and is inadequate for scenarios such as social media.

contributions.claim: The authors introduce behavior set and extend multi-behavior sequential recommendation to behavior set-informed sequential recommendation.
The authors propose EIDP, a dual-path transformer that separates explicit modeling from implicit modeling according to whether behavior representations are directly incorporated.

EIDP combines PBS-TPE for fine-grained intra-behavior dynamics, L-MSAB encoders for behavior-specific multi-view representations, and CBAF for behavior-level collaborative semantic fusion guided by the next behavior set.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe EIDP as a novel solution for behavior set-informed sequential recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of EIDP.
The authors report releasing implementation code for EIDP.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation and multi-behavior sequential recommendation arise from real-world scenarios, with multi-behavior recommendation modeling dependencies among behavior types.
Existing work is mainly studied in e-commerce, and conventional label-formatted behavior data is limited for settings such as social media.
The authors introduce behavior set and formulate behavior set-informed sequential recommendation, where dependencies are more complex and personalized.
They propose EIDP with explicit and implicit modeling paths and specialized modules for intra-behavior dynamics, behavior-specific representations, and cross-behavior fusion.
The abstract reports experiments on two real-world datasets and an implementation-code release.

source_observation.claim: Behavior types represented only as conventional labels may carry limited information in heterogeneous scenarios such as social media.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation models may need richer, set-level representations when behavior context is varied and behavior dependencies are personalized.

application.claim: For applications with heterogeneous user actions, consider modeling behavior sets and their intra-set dynamics rather than treating behavior types as isolated labels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether behavior-set modeling improves performance across domains beyond the reported two real-world datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, ablations, limitations, or error cases.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported effectiveness or code availability.
